Class RcxRegulatedDifferentialDrive

java.lang.Object
io.github.jabrena.juno.remote.lego.rcx.RcxRegulatedDifferentialDrive
public final class RcxRegulatedDifferentialDrive extends Object
A two-wheel RCX vehicle whose wheels are regulated on the brick: one RcxRegulatedPair on the firmware's only mapping (motor A with sensor 1 as the pair's left side, motor C with sensor 3 as its right side) driven by distance and heading through a RegulatedDifferentialDrive. It brings the RCX session, the regulator settings and the geometry together so a program configures one object, arms it, and moves it.

Create it once at startup, set the regulator (setTolerance(int), setTimeoutSeconds(int), setBrakeLead(int), setLinearSpeedMillimetresPerSecond(int)), then call tryArm() until the brick accepts the session. The settings the brick receives on arming apply from the next arm. Diagnostics, tachometers and the per-side motors stay on pair(); drive() is the board-independent drive, for composing it with other navigation such as a gyro-regulated drive.

  • Constructor Summary

    Constructors
    Constructor
    Description
    RcxRegulatedDifferentialDrive(RcxLink link, int session, int configurationFlags, int sensorStepsPerMotorRevolution, DriveGeometry geometry)
    Creates the drive over link for session (1..255), with the pair's configurationFlags (its INVERT_* and RcxRegulatedPair.BRAKE_ON_STOP bits and RcxRegulatedPair.maxPower(int)), the rotation sensor's steps per motor revolution, and the measured geometry.
    RcxRegulatedDifferentialDrive(RcxLink link, int session, int configurationFlags, int sensorStepsPerMotorRevolution, DriveGeometry geometry, boolean sidesSwapped)
    Creates the drive as RcxRegulatedDifferentialDrive(RcxLink, int, int, int, DriveGeometry) does; with sidesSwapped, the pair's left side (motor A) drives the robot's right wheel, so a counter-clockwise turn still turns counter-clockwise.

      public boolean tryArm()
